Which wearable breast pump is right for you?
There isn’t one best wearable breast pump. Match the job: warmth and massage, everyday pumping, a slimmer in-bra profile at work, app control with a quieter motor, or starting on a budget.
Wellness 1 warms the cup and adds massage with the suction rhythm, with three warmth levels at 37°C, 39°C and 41°C. App control, so you can adjust warmth and massage from your phone.
M5 Smart is the everyday wearable breast pump for most UK mums: app control, a 230 g cup, and suction up to −285 mmHg. Start here if you want an in-bra pump with a phone app and no extra hardware.
Air 1 is the slimmest all-in-one wearable at 61 mm, with a charging case for longer days out. Choose it when a lower in-bra profile matters under work clothes, especially if you’re pumping at work .
M9 is the quieter all-in-one wearable (≤42 dB), with app control, 15 suction levels and up to −300 mmHg. Pick it if you want finer control and a lower motor note.
M6 gives up to −300 mmHg without an app. Choose it if you want a simple daily wearable and you’d rather skip Bluetooth.
S12 Pro Quick is the entry all-in-one wearable if you want in-bra pumping at a lower price, with a 210 ml cup and a quicker clean.
All Momcozy pumps on this page
Use Type if you’re unsure. All-in-one wearable means tube-free: the motor sits in the cup. Separate unit, in-bra cups means collection cups in the bra and the motor outside.

Wearable, hands-free, wireless
Wearable, hands-free and wireless pumps
This is the UK shelf for in-bra pumps. Searches for hands-free or wireless usually mean a cup in your bra. Two formats: tube-free all-in-one, or collection cups with the motor outside.
Tube-free. Motor, flange and collector sit in the bra. On this page: Wellness 1, M5 Smart, Air 1, M9, M6, S12 Pro Quick and S9 Pro.
In the UK this usually means pumping without holding the flanges — an in-bra wearable. All-in-one cups and V1 Pro / V2 Pro collection cups both do that. Match the job in Best for.
No wall lead while you pump; the cup sits in your bra. Cordless is the same idea. Battery-powered electrics that are not in-bra sit on the Electric collection .
What to check on a wearable pump
Measure nipple diameter, not bra cup. Most Momcozy wearables include 17/19/21 mm inserts with a 24 mm flange. Pain, a white ring, or too much areola in the tunnel means resize before you turn suction up.
Check how the cup sits in a supportive pumping bra and whether you can lean forward a little. A poor seal is often fit or angle, not a reason to jump model.
Air 1 is the slimmest all-in-one at 61 mm. Choose that lower profile if you’re packing breastfeeding essentials for working mums and need the cup to sit flatter under work clothes.
Count the parts that touch milk and how quickly you can put the cup back together. A heated cup has extra parts. A wearable you dread washing will not stay your everyday pump.
Wellness 1 warms the cup to 37°C, 39°C or 41°C and adds massage with the suction rhythm. Warmth uses more charge — about 6 sessions with warmth, about 10 pumping only.
If you’re still choosing a breast pump in the UK , start with format: a tube-free all-in-one wearable, or a separate unit with in-bra collection cups. Then pick a model from Best for, or V1 Pro / V2 Pro above.
Which wearable breast pump is best?
There isn’t one best wearable breast pump. For warmth and massage, start with Wellness 1. For everyday pumping, M5 Smart. For working mums who need a slimmer in-bra profile, Air 1. For app control and a quieter motor, M9. M6 skips the app. S12 Pro Quick covers a lower price. Match the job rather than chasing a single winner.
What is a hands-free breast pump?
In the UK, a hands-free breast pump usually means an in-bra wearable, so you are not holding the flanges. That can be a tube-free all-in-one cup, or collection cups with the motor outside (V1 Pro or V2 Pro). There isn’t one best hands-free pump — match the job in Best for above.
What is a wireless breast pump?
A wireless breast pump, in UK search, usually means an in-bra cup with no wall lead while you pump. Cordless is the same idea. Those pumps sit on this page. Portable means battery-powered electric more broadly — that range is on the Electric collection.
Are V1 Pro and V2 Pro wearable pumps?
Yes. In the UK, wearable usually means the cups sit in your bra. V1 Pro and V2 Pro do that with a separate motor unit and in-bra collection cups. They are not all-in-one, tube-free wearables like M5 Smart or Air 1. Shop hospital-strength electric pumps if you want that format in more depth.
How should I store expressed milk in the UK?
Follow current NHS guidance. The NHS advises storing expressed milk in the fridge for up to 8 days at 4°C or lower, and in a freezer at −18°C or lower for up to 6 months. Some NHS pages also allow up to 6 hours at room temperature. Check the NHS expressing page before you rely on a figure.
Measure nipple diameter, not bra cup. Most Momcozy wearables include 17/19/21 mm inserts with a 24 mm flange. Pain, a white ring on the nipple, or too much areola being pulled in means resize before you turn suction up. Fit matters more than buying a “stronger” pump.
Do wearable pumps decrease milk supply?
Not if the cup empties the breast well. Supply

drops when the seal is poor, the flange is the wrong size, or sessions are too short or too infrequent — not because the motor sits in the bra. If output falls, check fit first, then session length. Speak to a midwife or lactation specialist if you’re worried about supply.
Can I exclusively use a wearable breast pump?
Yes, if it empties you comfortably and your output stays steady. Plenty of UK mums use an all-in-one wearable as their only pump. If you need longer sessions at home with the motor off the chest, V1 Pro and V2 Pro are on this page; the wider hospital-strength electric range is on the Electric collection.
Can I wear a regular bra while pumping?
A stretchy everyday bra can hold a cup if it is supportive enough to keep the seal. A dedicated pumping bra is more reliable for leaks and for leaning forward a little. If milk escapes, it is usually fit or angle, not a reason to jump model.
Does warmth and massage in a wearable pump help with let-down?
Some mums find in-cup warmth and a massage rhythm easier at the start of a session. Wellness 1 warms to 37°C, 39°C or 41°C. Warmth uses more battery — about 6 sessions with warmth, about 10 pumping only. It is a comfort feature, not a medical treatment. Speak to a midwife or lactation specialist if pumping is painful.
